title: EXAMPLE marker inside a provider-shaped value the provider did not publish
summary: Values that have a provider's documented prefix and a body of the right length and alphabet but whose body is the word EXAMPLE followed by filler: a Stripe sandbox secret key shape (sk_test_ then EXAMPLE and filler) and an AWS access key id shape (AKIA then EXAMPLE and filler). The provider published a different, exact example literal (AWS) or none (Stripe).
rationale: AWS publishes the exact pair AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE and wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY as examples, so those literals are documented examples. A value that only contains the same marker word is not that literal: nothing the provider wrote says a marker inside a body makes a value non-issuable. aws-example-keys-one-character-off already holds the exact-literal side for AWS under project policy. What stays open is a provider-shaped value with the marker word and no provider statement about it, where the marker could be a placeholder convention borrowed from AWS or a deliberate camouflage of a real key.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Settled (provider-documented): AWS prints AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE and wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY as examples of an access key ID and a secret access key; the statement is about those exact strings. Not settled: whether a different value carrying the word EXAMPLE is a placeholder; Stripe's key page read for this case says nothing about example markers. Missing: a provider statement about marker words, or a maintainer project-policy decision with named reviewer and dissent. The values are synthetic (a body of the marker word and filler; never issued); the provider-shaped prefix is why this is not a plain placeholder case. No product action is stated.

sources.supports: Access keys consist of an access key ID (for example, AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE) and a secret access key (for example, wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY); the page presents these two strings as examples.
